title: GPU Warm-Pool Cross-Account Handoff Runbook (2025)
author: Marisol Ortega
content:
Summary

This document describes the step-by-step oncall protocol for performing a cross-account GPU warm-pool handoff when the primary tenant capacity is exhausted and a burst to a secondary AWS account is required. It covers preflight checks, the handshake sequence between warm-pool-manager instances, IAM role-chain assumptions, emergency (time-boxed) IaC changes, verification, rollback, and observability.

This runbook is intended for oncall engineers (Infra SRE and GPU Fleet) who manage multi-account GPU bursting and warm-pool orchestration.

What changed in 2025 (read first)

- Triggering thresholds were tightened to reduce customer-facing tail latency.
- Handshake tokens now default to TTL 120 seconds (was 180s) due to replay-risk hardening.
- warmctl was renamed to gpuctl in the oncall bastion images (warmctl remains as a compatibility alias on some older regions).
- The cross-account role name changed to "redwood/gpu-warm-pool-handoff" (old name "redwood/warm-pool-handoff" still exists in a few legacy accounts; see IAM notes below).
- Router overrides are applied via router-admin (not direct /router/configs/apply) in most regions.

When to run this

- Automatic trigger: capacity-sentry signals BOTH:
  - sustained 90th-percentile queue time > 2.0s for 3 minutes (was 2.5s)
  - warm-pool saturation > 95% for 3 minutes
- Manual trigger: customer-facing latency incidents, region impairment, or when the allocation controller requests cross-account burst.

Preflight (5 minutes)

1) Confirm incident context and scope: affected tenant(s), region(s), and SLO impact.
2) Check SLO dashboard (tenant-specific):
   - 99th-pct latency target: 450ms token-serving (was 500ms)
   - Queue-time SLO: 95th-pct < 1.0s (was 1.2s)
3) Verify warm-pool health in both accounts: check warm-pool-manager metrics for:
   - active leases
   - available GPUs
   - preheat success rate
4) Confirm this is not a control-plane issue:
   - allocation-controller error rate
   - router-admin config push latency

Quick commands (run from the oncall bastion with appropriate MFA)

- Check capacity-sentry alerts:
  curl -s https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=capacity_sentry_alert

- List warm pool instances (k8s):
  kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=warm-pool-manager -o wide

- Inspect lease table:
  psql -h leases-db.internal -U infra_user -c "select * from leases where state in ('handshake','read_only') order by created_at desc limit 20;"

- Confirm gpuctl is available:
  which gpuctl || which warmctl

Roles and architecture notes

- warm-pool-manager: service running in every account responsible for preheating GPUs, tagging instances, and performing handshake.
- burst-orchestrator: global controller that decides the target account for overflow.
- capacity-sentry: SLO monitor and alerting signal source.
- xnet-egress: per-account egress proxy for cross-account traffic with bandwidth-aware shaping and compression (replaces egress-shim in most regions).
- lease-daemon: lightweight agent on compute nodes that accepts ephemeral leases and streams KV-cache seeds.
- router-admin: service that manages router sidecar route overrides and propagates configs.

Handshake protocol overview (high level)

1) burst-orchestrator determines target account and issues an ephemeral handshake token (default valid for 120 seconds; configurable).
2) warm-pool-manager in target account validates the token via IAM role chain and creates a placeholder Lease record in read-only state.
3) Source warm-pool-manager begins KV-cache seed transfer using the lease token and an mTLS-authenticated channel to the target account's lease-daemon.
4) After successful seed receipt, the target upgrades the Lease to Active and router-admin applies a route override so tenant requests flow to the new pool.

Detailed emergency handoff procedure (approx. 15–30 minutes)

Step 0 — Notify stakeholders (2 minutes)

- Announce on #infra-oncall and page the GPU Fleet oncall (PagerDuty) with priority P2.
- Include region, tenant(s), current queue time, warm-pool saturation, and whether this is multi-region.

Step 1 — Confirm IAM and trust boundary (3 minutes)

- Validate the target account has the cross-account role configured.
  - Preferred role name: "redwood/gpu-warm-pool-handoff"
  - Legacy role name (some accounts only): "redwood/warm-pool-handoff"

- Quick check (from source account):
  aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::TARGET_ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood/gpu-warm-pool-handoff --role-session-name handoff-check

- If assume-role fails:
  1) retry with legacy role name
  2) if still failing, escalate to cloud-accounts team (Slack: #cloud-accounts, oncall: @cloud-accounts). Do not proceed.

Step 2 — Issue ephemeral handshake token (1 minute)

- From burst-orchestrator console:
  POST /api/v1/handshake {"source_account":"A","target_account":"B","ttl_s":120}

- Record token id and TTL in the incident timeline.

Step 3 — Reserve capacity in target pool (3 minutes)

- In target account run one of the following (prefer gpuctl):
  kubectl -n infra exec deploy/warm-pool-manager -- /bin/gpuctl reserve --token <TOKEN_ID> --count <n_gpus>

- Sizing guidance:
  - Reserve predicted peak + 15% (was 10–20% above predicted peak); avoid over-reserving during partial incidents.

- If reserve fails due to account quotas, run the Quota quick path (below).

Step 4 — Seed transfer and KV-cache sync (6–12 minutes)

- Initiate transfer from source warm-pool-manager:
  /usr/local/bin/gpuctl transfer-seed --token <TOKEN_ID> --target-endpoint https://lease-daemon.target.internal:8443 --profile fast

- Watch transfer metrics in Prometheus:
  - warm_seed_transfer_duration_seconds
  - warm_seed_transfer_error_count
  - xnet_egress_bandwidth_utilization

- Expected durations:
  - 90% < 75s for a 4GB seed over inter-region link (with compression enabled)

- If transfer stalls > 150s (was 180s):
  1) reduce concurrent shards (--shards 4)
  2) retry once
  3) if repeated failures, abort and fall back to DNS-level routing (see Fallback options).

Step 5 — Activate lease and switch routing (2–4 minutes)

- On target:
  kubectl -n infra exec deploy/warm-pool-manager -- /bin/gpuctl activate --token <TOKEN_ID>

- Apply router override via router-admin (preferred):
  router-admin override set --tenant TENANT_ID --pool target-account-pool --ttl 30m

- Legacy (only if router-admin is unavailable in the region):
  POST /router/configs/apply with route override: route { tenant: "TENANT_ID", pool: "target-account-pool" }

- Wait for propagation:
  - typical: 60–90 seconds
  - if propagation exceeds 3 minutes, check router-admin backlog and config push error rate.

Verification (5 minutes)

- Confirm incoming requests are served from target pool:
  - sample last 100 requests and confirm trace header x-redwood-pool indicates target pool
- Confirm token billing tags and cost attribution are set:
  - check cost-annotator logs for token_id tag
- SLO check:
  - observe latency and queue-time dashboards for the affected tenant for a 10-minute window
  - expect queue-time to drop by >= 40% after routing changes stabilize

Rollback and fallback options

- If KV-cache transfer fails irrecoverably:
  - run fallback DNS-level routing to a best-effort cached model in a regional pool:
    /usr/local/bin/gpuctl fallback-dns --tenant TENANT_ID --region REGION_CODE

- To fully rollback (deactivate target pool):
  kubectl -n infra exec deploy/warm-pool-manager -- /bin/gpuctl deactivate --token <TOKEN_ID> --force

- Post-rollback:
  - ensure lease state in leases-db is set to "aborted"
  - add trace ids and token id to the incident record

Quota quick path (when target reservation fails)

1) Check current quota:
   aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-ABCDEFGH --region <REGION>

2) If instantaneous quota bump is configured (emergency-bump role):
   aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::TARGET_ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood/instant-quota-bump --role-session-name qb

3) Execute the emergency bump:
   - Preferred path (2025): run the quota-bumper workflow:
     quota-bumper run --account TARGET_ACCOUNT_ID --region REGION --delta-gpu +X --reason "GPU warm-pool handoff"
   - Legacy path (only if workflow unavailable): Terraform apply against iac/quotas/emergency-bump.tf with variables:
     --var 'account=TARGET_ACCOUNT_ID' --var 'delta_gpu=+X' and set -auto-approve.

Only the cloud-accounts engineer should execute quota bumps; page them if necessary.

Observability and dashboards (ongoing)

- Prometheus metrics to watch:
  - warm_pool_active_leases{account,region} (target should increase)
  - warm_seed_transfer_rate_bytes
  - capacity_sentry_queue_time_seconds
  - xnet_egress_bandwidth_utilization
  - router_admin_apply_duration_seconds

- Logs:
  - lease-daemon logs (stdout) aggregated in kibana index leases-logs-*/_search
  - look for "seed-received" and "seed-commit" events

- Traces:
  - sampling key x-redwood-trace-token in Jaeger should show cross-account hops

Post-incident tasks (owner: GPU Fleet)

1) Create a postmortem within 48 hours if the handoff was non-trivial or if SLOs were missed. Include timeline and seed-transfer traces.
2) If quota bumps were used, reconcile cost center tags and submit billing adjustment within 5 business days.
3) If transfer retries occurred >2x, open a backlog ticket for transfer optimization and include transfer artifacts (logs, histogram).

Security considerations

- Handshake tokens are single-use and TTL-limited (default 120s). Never paste tokens into external channels.
- All cross-account transfers must happen over mTLS endpoints; confirm certificate fingerprint before starting (see cert-check below).
- Do not run routing overrides without an incident ticket id in the override description/annotation.

Cert check (one-liner)

- openssl s_client -connect lease-daemon.target.internal:8443 -servername lease-daemon.target.internal | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256
- Confirm fingerprint matches entry in keyring:
  kubectl -n infra get configmap handoff-keyring -o yaml | grep <fingerprint>

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: GPU Fleet (PagerDuty alias: #gpu-fleet-oncall)
- Secondary: cloud-accounts (Slack: #cloud-accounts)
- Networking: #infra-networking
- Escalation path:
  - after 10 minutes of blocked handoff, escalate to SRE manager
  - start a P1 bridge if customer impact is P1 or if >1 enterprise tenant is impacted

Change control and IaC notes

- Any permanent changes to the handoff role, token TTL defaults, or the transfer protocol must be implemented in Terraform and go through infra GitHub repo CI/CD gates.
- PR requirements:
  - unit test for token TTL enforcement
  - integration test that mocks assume-role
  - canary rollout policy for gpuctl binary

- Emergency IaC patch (only cloud-accounts):
  - update terraform/modules/iam/roles.tf
  - run: terraform plan -var 'account=TARGET_ACCOUNT_ID' && terraform apply -auto-approve
  - run terraform fmt and policy-as-code checks before apply unless explicitly waived by cloud-accounts oncall during an active incident

Appendix: common failure modes and remediation

| Symptom | Probable cause | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seed transfer stalls at 0% | xnet-egress throttling or misrouted endpoint | Reduce shards; ensure correct lease-daemon endpoint; contact networking if sustained >5min |
| Assume-role fails | Missing trust policy or SCP denial | Validate role ARN; check org SCP; escalate to cloud-accounts |
| Router override not applied | router-admin backlog or propagation error | Reapply override; check router-admin queue depth; restart router sidecar only as last resort |

Change history

- 2025-02-08: Clarified quota quick path and added cert-check (Ethan Kwan reviewer)
- 2025-11-03: 2025 refresh: gpuctl rename, token TTL default 120s, tighter triggers, router-admin override path, xnet-egress naming (Sofia Almeida reviewer)

Related reading

- GPU capacity runway and warm-pool sizing whitepaper for sizing heuristics.
- xnet-egress operational runbook for bandwidth shaping and compression settings.
- IAM role naming and session policy standard.

Contact matrix

- gpu-fleet-oncall: pagerduty/@gpu-fleet-oncall
- cloud-accounts: slack/#cloud-accounts
- networking: slack/#infra-networking

End of runbook
